title: Pad Krapow Gai
subtitle: Thai holy basil chicken. 5 min prep, 8 min cook.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Ask the Tops/Villa butcher to mince it — faster and far less cleanup. Thigh is more forgiving than breast at high heat.

ingredients.note: One egg per serving, fried in the same pan after the chicken.
Oil cap — do not exceed. Split: half for chicken, half for eggs.
Pound with the chilies in a mortar — don't fine-mince.

ingredients.item: Thai bird's eye chili (prik kee noo)
ingredients.note: Halve or skip for mild. Fresh markets sell them by the bag.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Maekrua or Lee Kum Kee — both fine. Maekrua is the local default.
Healthy Boy brand, dark soy aisle. Adds the brown lacquer colour.
MUST be holy basil (bai krapow), not sweet Thai basil (bai horapha). Fresh markets only — supermarket bags are usually horapha. If you can't find krapow, this is pad horapha, not pad krapow.

ingredients.note: Splash to deglaze and emulsify the sauce.

substitutions.note: Higher protein, leaner. Easier to overcook — pull from heat the moment it loses pink.
The traditional version is pork (pad krapow moo). Slightly fattier.
Lose the runny yolk but cut fat. Less satisfying.

steps.text: Pound garlic + chilies in mortar to rough paste. No mortar: smash flat with side of knife, then chop.
Heat 1/2 tsp oil in non-stick wok or pan, high. Add garlic-chili paste, stir 15 sec until fragrant.
Add minced chicken. Break up, press flat, leave 30 sec to brown, then stir-fry until no pink, ~4 min.
Add oyster sauce, fish sauce, dark soy, sugar, stock. Toss to coat. Cook 1 min until glossy.
Kill heat. Throw in holy basil, toss twice — leaves should wilt from residual heat, not cook.
Plate. Wipe pan, add remaining 1/2 tsp oil on high, crack eggs and fry hard — crispy edges, runny yolk. Slide onto each plate.

serves_with.note: Standard. Adds ~200 kcal / 43g carbs per pack.

notes: Real pad krapow lives or dies on the basil. Holy basil (krapow) is peppery, almost clove-like — sweet Thai basil (horapha) is anise-y and wrong for this dish. The fried egg with runny yolk is non-negotiable; the yolk is the sauce. Pound the garlic and chilies — don't mince — for the right rough texture.
